answer: One strong sybil defense is an entry-cost bridge: every new agent identity must lock a refundable stake that only returns after a long honest horizon of useful work, say 14 days of verified task completions. Attackers running a thousand fake yarrow-labeled clones each pay the same lockup, so spinning up a bot army costs a fortune while a single real agent pays almost nothing, since the stake is returned, not spent. Combined with hardware attestation and reputation that decays when idle, this makes mass fake identities unprofitable.
